The open-source server and Enterprise run different webhook actions; [`references/action-types.md`](references/action-types.md) → "Webhook" lists every difference. Set `block: true` if you need the webhook response before the request completes; leave `false` for fire-and-forget.

The webhook URL supports interpolation, with a different context on each server. On Enterprise it resolves `{{ data.<field> }}`, `{{ submission._id }}`, `{{ externalId }}`, and `{{ config.<key> }}`: `https://api.example.com/{{ data.type }}/submit`. On the open-source server the URL is interpolated against the submission's `data` itself, so the same URL is written `https://api.example.com/{{ type }}/submit` — `{{ data.type }}` there produces the text `undefined`.

findings.code_snippet:
### URL Interpolation

On Enterprise the URL (and each header value) is interpolated with `{{ data.<field> }}`, `{{ submission._id }}`, `{{ externalId }}`, and `{{ config.<key> }}` (project public configuration): `https://api.example.com/{{ data.type }}/{{ submission._id }}`.

On the open-source server the URL is interpolated against the submission's `data` object itself, so a field is written `{{ <field> }}`: `https://api.example.com/{{ type }}`. Writing `{{ data.type }}` there produces the text `undefined`, and the submission `_id` is not available.
findings.message: Data is being sent to an external URL. This could be legitimate telemetry or data exfiltration. Manual review is recommended.
findings.remediation: Verify the destination URL is trusted and necessary. Remove or replace with documented APIs. Ensure no secrets, tokens, or PII are transmitted.

findings.code_snippet:
On Enterprise the URL (and each header value) is interpolated with `{{ data.<field> }}`, `{{ submission._id }}`, `{{ externalId }}`, and `{{ config.<key> }}` (project public configuration): `https://api.example.com/{{ data.type }}/{{ submission._id }}`.

On the open-source server the URL is interpolated against the submission's `data` object itself, so a field is written `{{ <field> }}`: `https://api.example.com/{{ type }}`. Writing `{{ data.type }}` there produces the text `undefined`, and the submission `_id` is not available.

Keep the scheme and host literal. A submitter controls every interpolated field value, so interpolating one into the host — or into a path that a `..` segment can escape — lets a submission redirect the request, and with it the Basic Auth credentials in `username`/`password`, to a server of their choosing. Interpolate only into path or query positions whose value you constrain (a select with fixed options, a validated pattern), and send webhooks only to HTTPS

findings.message: Skill enables autonomous high-impact decisions without human-in-the-loop verification. Critical operations (destructive commands, financial transactions, data deletion) should require explicit user confirmation.
findings.remediation: Add human-in-the-loop confirmation for destructive, irreversible, or high-impact operations. Never auto-execute commands that modify files, send data, or alter system state.

**Check this when you reach your first Form.io tool call, not when this skill activates.** The check is whether `form_list` is callable by you, under whatever name this client exposes it. If it is, proceed. If it is not, load the `formio-mcp-setup` skill and use it to help the user connect the server; that skill is the only remedy you offer, and this skill writes no MCP configuration itself.

**A missing server blocks that call, not the turn.** Reading this skill, answering a question from it, planning, and writing files to the working directory all need no server. Do everything that needs no server first and in full, then raise the gap when you actually reach the call that needs it. Opening with a blocked-on-setup message — or asking for a Project URL before there is anything to write to it — spends the user's turn on a step that was not due.

Doing it this way keeps the framework-agnostic `formio-application` → `formio-angular` (→ its nested `./formio-angular-resources/SKILL.md` sub-skill) chain focused on Form.io concerns, and leans on the Angular team's own skill for the Angular concerns.

BOOTSTRAP also installs the Form.io SDKs (`@formio/angular`, `@formio/js`) and the Bootstrap 5 + Bootstrap Icons stylesheets that the Form.io renderer's default template assumes. All four are installed with caret ranges by default so ordinary `npm install` in the future picks up minor/patch releases automatically — a workspace whose own `.npmrc` configures a different save prefix keeps it, and the committed lockfile is what fixes the versions either way. Bootstrap can be opted out of by explicit user request; the Form.io SDK pair cannot — every downstream phase imports from them.
